Package neqsim.process.equipment.distillation

Class MeshStageDerivatives

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.distillation.MeshStageDerivatives
final class MeshStageDerivatives extends Object
Analytic derivatives of the equilibrium-stage quantities used by the simultaneous-correction column solver.

The stage variables are the liquid component flows l_m, the temperature T and the total vapor flow V. The K-values are defined implicitly by ln K_i = ln phiL_i(T, x) - ln phiV_i(T, y) with x_i = l_i / L and y_i = K_i x_i / sum(K x). Differentiating this fixed point gives the linear system (I + AV diag(y)) dlnK = (BL - BV) dT + (AL - AV diag(K / s)) dl / L, where A and B are the composition and temperature derivatives of ln phi of the liquid (L) and vapor (V) phases and s is sum(K x). The terms that come from normalizing the compositions vanish because ln phi is homogeneous of degree zero in the mole numbers.

Enthalpy derivatives use the heat capacity and the partial molar enthalpies hbar_i = h_i^ig(T) - R T^2 dln(phi_i)/dT. One evaluation of each phase with composition derivatives replaces the C + 2 perturbed stage evaluations of a finite-difference Jacobian, and the result is exact to rounding instead of to the perturbation size.

Derivative arrays are indexed by stage variable: 0..C-1 are the liquid component flows, C is the temperature and C + 1 is the total vapor flow.

  • Method Details

    • loadPhase

      boolean loadPhase(SystemInterface system, boolean vapor)
      Read the fugacity and enthalpy derivatives of one phase.

      The work system holds one mole at the stage temperature, pressure and composition. Initialize it at level 3 after checking the model supplies both required fugacity derivatives. Reject the phase when the derivatives are not finite, when the composition derivatives are not homogeneous of degree zero, or when the mole-fraction weighted partial molar enthalpies do not reproduce the phase enthalpy. A rejected phase means the thermodynamic model does not supply the derivatives this class needs, and the caller must use finite differences.

      Parameters:
      system - one-mole work system configured with the forced phase root
      vapor - true to store the values as the vapor phase, false for the liquid phase
      Returns:
      true when the derivatives are finite and consistent
